quizzes.stem: A team lead wants an assistant to prepare a weekly status email from a spreadsheet of task progress notes. The email goes to executives. Which division of work is soundest?

options.a: Claude writes the first version; a person verifies facts and approves sending
options.b: A person writes the email; Claude only corrects spelling and grammar
options.c: Claude drafts and also decides which blockers to escalate to executives
options.d: Claude collects the notes, writes the email and sends it, with spot checks later

explanation.a: Drafting is language-shaped and reviewable, while checking facts and approving the send stay with a person (the worked example's table).
explanation.d: Ruled out because the table keeps "Check every figure in the draft against the source" with a person or a script, and spot checks later come after readers have the email.
explanation.b: Ruled out because Claude "saves the time spent on prose", the main saving, which a person writing everything forgoes.
explanation.c: Ruled out because escalation is "judgment that carries accountability", which stays with a person.

quizzes.stem: Someone asks Claude: "Summarise this report." The result is accurate, but the sales team who asked cannot use it. Which gap in the request most likely caused this?

options.a: It lacked a role line naming Claude an expert summariser
options.b: It omitted a word limit, which is why the summary missed the sales angle
options.c: It never said who would read it or what they must decide with it
options.d: It ran on a tier too small to judge what matters to sales

explanation.c: The description should cover the goal and the context, who reads it and why, and a generic request gets a generic reply.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a role line names no reader or purpose, and the page says to "Add what a colleague new to the job would need".
explanation.b: Ruled out because without the goal "Claude cannot choose between reasonable readings", and a limit is only a constraint on form.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the description is where most of the quality is decided", and a larger tier does not know the readers either.

quizzes.stem: An analyst asks Claude to summarise a regulation for compliance colleagues. The summary cites "subsection 14(b)(ii)" for a retention rule, and the analyst is about to forward it. What is the most appropriate step?

options.a: Ask Claude whether it is confident, and forward the summary if it says yes
options.b: Look the passage up in the source of record before sending it on
options.c: Ask Claude to cite the subsection again in a fresh reply and compare the two
options.d: Forward it with a note that an AI drafted it, so readers can judge

explanation.b: Specific citations are the kind of detail a model can invent, so the claim that would hurt if wrong is checked against the source of record (the checking routine).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the routine says that asking the model how sure it is, or "for its confidence does not verify anything".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the routine says to check "against the source of record, not against the model", and a second reply from the same model is not the source.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Check in proportion to the cost of being wrong", and a note about an AI draft leaves the unchecked claim in place.

quizzes.stem: A competitor table has one cell marked "data unavailable" while every other cell is filled. A colleague asks you to drop that row so the table looks finished. Which response is best?

options.a: Ask Claude to try again until every cell holds a value
options.b: Fill it with a typical industry figure and label it an estimate
options.c: Show a dash in that cell and drop any mention of the missing data
options.d: Retain the entry as it stands and state what could not be located

explanation.d: A declared gap is information, and the careful move is to keep it and decide what to do (the spotting a gap section).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Regenerating the same request and hoping is the reflex", and pressing for a value invites invention.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the careless move is to fill the gap with an estimate".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says "Keep the gap and decide what to do about it", not hide it behind a dash.

quizzes.stem: A team uses Claude to draft a monthly variance narrative from a finance export. After a few clean months the lead proposes two changes: Claude will also decide which variances reach the directors, and the figure-by-figure review stops. Which response applies both pages?

options.a: Keep the judgment call with a person and keep verifying every number against its source
options.b: Let Claude take the judgment call, since clean drafts show sound judgment, and keep verifying
options.c: Drop the verification, since clean drafts show the numbers are right, and keep the judgment call
options.d: Let Claude take both, and ask it to flag any figure it is unsure of

explanation.a: Judgment that carries accountability stays with a person, and figures are checked against the source of record however clean past drafts were (page 1 delegation table; page 2 checking routine).
explanation.b: Ruled out because because the table gives "Decide which variances matter to the board" to a person, as judgment with accountability, and a clean run does not move it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because because "A good draft does not show the figures were right", so a run of clean drafts is no reason to stop verifying.
explanation.d: Ruled out because because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy", and a flag from the model replaces neither the person nor the check.

quizzes.stem: A support lead gets a drafted reply to an angry customer that is accurate but reads like a legal notice. The lead needs the next attempt to come out right. Which change to the request follows the pages?

options.a: Open with a role line: "You are a world-class customer-care writer"
options.b: Send the identical request again and keep the first answer that sounds friendly
options.c: Describe the audience, add one sample in the voice wanted, then compare
options.d: Move to a higher tier, which follows loose instructions better

explanation.c: The description should say who reads it and show the target style, and the iterate-not-re-roll method compares the new result with the last (page 1, describe; page 2, iterate).
explanation.b: Ruled out because because "Regenerating the same request and hoping is the reflex", and an identical request is a second guess.
explanation.a: Ruled out because because a role line names no reader or purpose, and the page says to "Add what a colleague new to the job would need".
explanation.d: Ruled out because because "the description is where most of the quality is decided", and a higher tier does not know the readers either.

quizzes.stem: A consultant forwards a client a report that Claude drafted. The client later finds a wrong number in it. Who answers for the mistake, and what should have happened first?

options.a: The tool's provider answers, since its software produced the number
options.b: The sender owns the work and should have verified the figures at their source
options.c: The recipient answers, since the number was accepted without question
options.d: The sender answers, but only if the work lacked a note about the AI's part

explanation.b: The sender owns what was sent, and figures are checked against the source of record before release (page 2, take responsibility and the checking routine; page 1, where checking every figure sits with a person or a script).
explanation.a: Ruled out because because "You own what you send, whoever drafted it".
explanation.c: Ruled out because because "the person who relied on it will not distinguish between you and the tool", so blame does not move to the reader.
explanation.d: Ruled out because because "An error in AI-assisted work is your error to correct", with or without a disclosure note; disclosure is a separate duty.

quizzes.stem: A team asks Claude to fill a supplier price table from a PDF. The result has every row filled, including a cost the PDF never states. Which pair of actions fits both pages?

options.a: Check only the layout and tone of the result, and accept the data as given
options.b: Ask it to give a confidence beside each entry, and keep the ones it marks high
options.c: Tell it to leave no cell empty, and label the invented entries as estimates
options.d: Tell it to say so when a value is absent instead of estimating, and keep any gap it reports

explanation.d: Page 1 puts the rule in the description ("say so rather than estimating"), and page 2 says a declared gap is information to keep.
explanation.b: Ruled out because because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".
explanation.c: Ruled out because because "the careless move is to fill the gap with an estimate", and a label on an invented value still puts it in the table.
explanation.a: Ruled out because because "Readers check tone and grammar, which are visible, and skip figures and citations", which is where the damage is.
